name: Ceftazidime
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ceftazidime is removed almost entirely by glomerular filtration (80% to 90% unchanged in urine). The US label gives a 1 g loading dose, then reduced maintenance doses when creatinine clearance (CrCl) is 50 mL/min or less, 1 g after each hemodialysis, and 500 mg daily on peritoneal dialysis. High levels in kidney impairment can cause seizures and encephalopathy.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault); the text refers to GFR <50 mL/min.
chip: CrCl ≤50: reduce; 1 g after each HD

bands.recommendation: CrCl 51–59: usual dose. CrCl 31–50: 1 g every 12 hours (label Table 4). Loading dose 1 g; if the usual dose (label Table 3) is lower, use the lower dose; in severe infections the unit dose may be raised by 50% or the interval shortened (label).

CrCl 16–30: 1 g every 24 hours; CrCl 15: 500 mg every 24 hours (label Table 4). Loading dose 1 g; if the usual dose (label Table 3) is lower, use the lower dose; in severe infections the unit dose may be raised by 50% or the interval shortened (label).

CrCl 6–15: 500 mg every 24 hours; below 5: 500 mg every 48 hours (label Table 4; 5 itself not specified). Loading dose 1 g; if the usual dose (label Table 3) is lower, use the lower dose; in severe infections the unit dose may be raised by 50% or the interval shortened (label).

hd: Loading dose 1 g, then 1 g after each hemodialysis period (label). Literature option (not label): thrice-weekly after each session, 1 g, 1 g and 2 g for organisms with MIC of 8 µg/mL or less, or 2 g, 2 g and 3 g for Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Tsai 2025). These regimens are not weight-adjusted and come mostly from small pharmacokinetic studies; confirm the actual last and next session before each dose. See the site guide Antibiotic Stewardship in Hemodialysis (/guides/antibiotic-stewardship-dialysis.html).
pd: Label: intraperitoneal dialysis or CAPD, loading dose 1 g, then 500 mg every 24 hours; ceftazidime can also be added to dialysis fluid at 250 mg per 2 L (label). For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal intermittent 1,000 to 1,500 mg daily (long dwell) or 20 mg/kg daily (short dwell); continuous loading dose 500 mg/L, then 125 mg/L in each exchange. Continuous cephalosporin doses may need about 25% more in patients with significant residual kidney function (ISPD 2022).
crrt: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) lists only ceftazidime-avibactam, not ceftazidime alone. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Yes: hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis may aid removal (label overdose section). Less than 10% protein bound.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus, encephalopathy, asterixis and myoclonia with high levels in kidney impairment (label); kidney function with aminoglycosides or loop diuretics.

pediatric.approved_ages: Neonates (0 to 4 weeks) and children (label dose table).
pediatric.usual_dose: 1 month to 12 years: 30 to 50 mg/kg IV every 8 hours (higher dose for immunocompromised children, cystic fibrosis or meningitis) (label).
pediatric.neonates: 0 to 4 weeks: 30 mg/kg IV every 12 hours (label).

renal.recommendation: Adjust CrCl for body surface area or lean body mass and reduce dosing frequency as in adults (label). No pediatric table.
